note: Curated career tracks. Interview questions are taken from interview_question_bank.json and learning topics from learning_plans.json at request time. Resources are official documentation sites only.

tracks.title: Software Developer
tracks.summary: Builds and maintains applications: writes clean, tested code, works with databases and APIs, and collaborates through version control.

roadmap.goal: Write small programs confidently and keep them in Git.
Solve common coding problems and build a database-backed API.
Package, test and ship your code automatically.

exercises: Implement a stack, queue and hash map from scratch and write unit tests for each.
Solve 20 easy and 10 medium array/string problems, noting the time complexity of each solution.
Design the tables for a library system and write SQL for borrowing and returning books.
projects: A task-manager REST API with authentication, a database and automated tests.
A command-line tool that parses log files and reports statistics, published with a README.
resume_advice: List languages and tools in a Skills section and show each one in a project.
Describe projects with the problem, your solution and a measurable result.
Link to a GitHub profile with clean, documented repositories.

tracks.title: AI Engineer
tracks.summary: Turns machine-learning models (including language models) into reliable product features: data pipelines, model integration, evaluation and deployment.

roadmap.goal: Train and evaluate classic models on real datasets.
Build and fine-tune neural networks for text tasks.
Serve a model behind an API and deploy it.

exercises: Train a text classifier and report precision, recall and F1 on a held-out set.
Write an evaluation script that compares two models on the same test data.
Wrap a trained model in a small HTTP API with input validation.
projects: A document question-answering service that retrieves relevant passages before answering, with an evaluation set.
A sentiment-analysis API, containerised with Docker, with a short write-up of its accuracy and limits.
resume_advice: Report model metrics and the dataset size for every AI project.
Show the engineering side: APIs, tests, deployment, not only notebooks.
Name the frameworks (PyTorch, scikit-learn) in each project description.

tracks.title: Machine Learning Engineer
tracks.summary: Designs, trains and maintains machine-learning models and the pipelines that feed and serve them.

roadmap.goal: Handle data and reason about distributions and errors.
Build, validate and compare supervised models.
Train neural networks and package models for reuse.

exercises: Implement linear regression with NumPy and compare it with scikit-learn's result.
Run k-fold cross-validation and explain over- and under-fitting from the results.
Write a feature pipeline that handles missing values and categorical columns.
projects: An end-to-end prediction project: data cleaning, model selection, evaluation and a reproducible training script.
A model-monitoring report that compares predictions on new data with the training data.
resume_advice: Quantify results (accuracy, error reduction) and state the baseline you beat.
Mention data size and how you validated the model.
Separate tools (scikit-learn, TensorFlow) from concepts (regression, classification).

tracks.title: Data Scientist
tracks.summary: Answers business questions with data: exploration, statistics, modelling and clear communication of results.

roadmap.goal: Query, summarise and test hypotheses on data.
Clean and explore real datasets and present findings.
Build predictive models and explain them to non-experts.

exercises: Clean a messy CSV with pandas and document every transformation.
Run and interpret an A/B test with a confidence interval.
Write five SQL queries using joins, grouping and window functions on a sample dataset.
projects: An exploratory analysis of a public dataset with a written summary of three insights.
A churn or demand prediction model with feature importance and a plain-language explanation.
resume_advice: Lead with the question you answered and the impact of the answer.
Show both analysis (SQL, pandas) and communication (dashboards, reports).
Mention the statistical methods you used.

tracks.title: Data Analyst
tracks.summary: Turns raw data into reports and dashboards that help teams make decisions.

roadmap.goal: Clean data and answer questions with spreadsheets and queries.
Build dashboards that track business metrics.
Automate analysis and test whether changes are significant.

exercises: Build a pivot-table report and a chart from a sales dataset in Excel.
Write SQL to compute monthly revenue, growth and top products.
Design a one-page dashboard with three KPIs and a filter.
projects: A sales or operations dashboard in Tableau or Power BI with a short guide for its users.
An automated weekly report generated from SQL and Python.
resume_advice: Name the tools (SQL, Excel, Tableau/Power BI) and what you built with each.
Quantify the decisions your analysis supported.
Include a link to a public dashboard if you have one.

tracks.title: Web Developer
tracks.summary: Builds responsive, accessible websites and web applications, from the user interface to the APIs behind it.

roadmap.goal: Build accessible, responsive pages without a framework.
Build component-based apps with state and routing.
Connect your front end to your own API and database.

exercises: Build a responsive landing page that passes an accessibility check.
Fetch data from an API in React and handle loading, empty and error states.
Add form validation with clear error messages.
projects: A full-stack app (React + Node.js or similar) with authentication and a database.
A personal portfolio site, deployed, with case studies of your projects.
resume_advice: Link to live demos and source code.
Mention accessibility and performance work explicitly.
Show both front-end and back-end skills if you have them.

tracks.title: Java Developer
tracks.summary: Builds back-end services and applications in Java, typically with Spring Boot and relational databases.

roadmap.goal: Write object-oriented Java with collections and tests.
Build a database-backed REST service.
Package and test your service automatically.

exercises: Model a small domain (e.g. orders) with classes, interfaces and unit tests.
Build CRUD endpoints with Spring Boot and validate the input.
Write a query that joins three tables and map the result to Java objects.
projects: A Spring Boot REST API with a relational database, tests and API documentation.
A multi-module Java application with a clear package structure and a build pipeline.
resume_advice: State the Java version and frameworks you used.
Describe API design and testing, not only features.
Show database work (schema design, queries).

tracks.title: Python Developer
tracks.summary: Builds back-end services, automation and data tools in Python.

roadmap.goal: Write idiomatic, tested Python packages.
Build and document database-backed APIs.
Deploy and run Python services.

exercises: Write a module with type hints, docstrings and pytest tests.
Build a FastAPI endpoint with request validation and error handling.
Automate a repetitive task (file renaming, report generation) with a script.
projects: A FastAPI or Django service with authentication, a database and tests.
An automation tool that saves a measurable amount of manual work, with a README.
resume_advice: Name the frameworks and show tests in your projects.
Mention automation results in time saved.
Keep a tidy GitHub with installable packages.

tracks.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
tracks.summary: Protects systems and data: monitors for threats, investigates incidents and helps fix vulnerabilities.

roadmap.goal: Understand how networks and operating systems work and fail.
Detect, investigate and report security issues.
Automate checks and secure cloud resources.

exercises: Capture and explain the traffic of a web request (DNS, TCP, HTTP).
Review a sample web app against the OWASP Top 10 and write findings.
Write a script that flags suspicious lines in an authentication log.
projects: A home-lab write-up: a monitored network with documented detection of a simulated attack.
A security assessment report of a deliberately vulnerable practice application.
resume_advice: List labs and practice platforms you completed, with what you learned.
Show written reports: clear communication matters in security.
Mention relevant certifications you hold or are preparing for.

tracks.title: Cloud Engineer
tracks.summary: Designs, builds and operates infrastructure on cloud platforms, preferably as code.

roadmap.goal: Administer servers and understand cloud networking basics.
Deploy applications on a cloud provider.
Provision and observe infrastructure reproducibly.

exercises: Deploy a static website on a cloud provider using its free tier.
Write Terraform for a network, a server and a security group.
Set up an alert when a server's CPU stays high.
projects: A web app deployed with Terraform, including networking, a database and monitoring.
A cost and architecture write-up of a small cloud deployment.
resume_advice: Name the cloud services you used and why.
Show infrastructure as code in public repositories.
Mention cloud certifications you hold or are preparing for.

tracks.title: DevOps Engineer
tracks.summary: Automates how software is built, tested, deployed and monitored.

roadmap.goal: Work comfortably on the command line and with branches.
Build and test every change automatically.
Deploy, scale and observe services.

exercises: Write a pipeline that runs tests and builds a container image on every push.
Write a Dockerfile for a web app and reduce the image size.
Deploy a container to a local Kubernetes cluster with a health check.
projects: A complete CI/CD pipeline for a sample app: build, test, containerise and deploy.
A monitoring dashboard with alerts for a deployed service.
resume_advice: Describe pipelines you built and what they improved (speed, reliability).
List tools by stage: build, deploy, monitor.
Link to repositories with pipeline configuration.

tracks.title: Frontend Developer
tracks.summary: Builds the parts of web applications people see and use: accessible, responsive interfaces that talk to APIs.

roadmap.goal: Build semantic, responsive pages and add interactivity without a framework.
Build a typed single-page app from reusable components, kept in Git.
Load data from APIs, handle loading/error states and compare frameworks.

exercises: Rebuild a landing page from a screenshot with semantic HTML and a mobile-first layout.
Write a debounce function and a fetch wrapper with error handling in plain JavaScript.
Build a React form with validation, keyboard support and error messages linked to inputs.
projects: A responsive dashboard in React and TypeScript that loads data from a public API with loading, empty and error states.
An accessible component library (button, modal, tabs) with keyboard support and documentation.
resume_advice: Link a live demo and the repository for each front-end project.
Mention accessibility, responsiveness and performance work explicitly.
Name the framework, language and styling approach used in each project.

tracks.title: Backend Developer
tracks.summary: Builds the server side of applications: APIs, databases, authentication and the business logic behind them.

roadmap.goal: Write clean server-side code and manage it in Git.
Design a relational schema and expose it through a validated REST API.
Containerise a service, run it on Linux and learn a full framework.

exercises: Design tables for an online shop and write SQL with joins, grouping and an index.
Build a REST endpoint with input validation, pagination and proper status codes.
Add password hashing and token-based sign-in to a small API and test both.
projects: A REST API for a booking system with authentication, a relational database and automated tests.
A background job that imports a CSV file into a database and reports errors, packaged with Docker.
resume_advice: Describe the API, the database and how you tested them for each project.
Mention security work such as authentication, validation or rate limiting.
Quantify results honestly (requests handled, query time reduced) only where you measured them.

tracks.title: Full Stack Developer
tracks.summary: Builds complete web applications end to end: the interface, the API and the database, and ships them.

roadmap.goal: Build an interactive, responsive interface from components.
Serve data from a database through a REST API you designed.
Type the whole app, keep it in Git and run it in a container.

exercises: Connect a React form to an API endpoint that saves to a database and shows server errors in the form.
Write SQL for a one-to-many relationship and expose it as nested JSON from an API.
Add sign-in to a small full-stack app and protect one page and one endpoint.
projects: A full-stack task or notes app with sign-in, a database, an API and a React front end, deployed with instructions.
A small e-commerce catalogue with search, filters and an admin page for adding products.
resume_advice: Show which parts you built: front end, API, database, deployment.
Link the live app and the repository with a clear README.
List the stack per project rather than one long list of tools.
